title: MergeReadinessVerdict
description: Output of the Merge Judge: an independent decision, after the reviewer/implementer exchange has settled, on whether the change is ready for a human to review on the forge. Consumes the spec, findings, responses, test results, and the deterministic checks. Never edits code.

result.description: ready: open the change request. another_round: send back to implementer with the listed findings. escalate: the loop is not converging or a decision needs a human.

judge_assessment.description: The judge's own view of who is right, with reasoning. Judges the exchange, not just the code.

criteria.description: One row per acceptance criterion in the spec: the judge's own verdict on it, from evidence the judge located (a test in test_results.json or the diff, an orchestrator e2e row whose covers_ac names the criterion, a reproduction the judge ran). This table, not the reviewer's spec_conformance, is what the change request renders. not_assessed is reserved for a criterion nobody could exercise (the service would not start from its manifest entrypoint, or the only evidence needs a platform this run lacks); where the orchestrator's e2e rows exist for it, the criterion is met or not_met.

evidence.description: Where the proof is: test id and result, test_results.json e2e row (command, exit code, target), or the probe the judge ran.

deterministic_checks.description: Results the orchestrator computed and handed to the judge. The judge may not override a failing deterministic check.

pr_summary.description: The part of the verdict the change request description shows, written for an engineer who knows the app and nothing about the factory: third person, plain words, no ids (criteria, findings, checks, sessions), no agent names, no costs. The judge never sees the description and does not comment on it. Post-mortem 2026-10-11 §5.

what_changed.description: Two to four sentences: what the change does for its users and why.

how_tested.description: One or two sentences on what the tests and browser checks cover, in the app's terms. The controller adds the counts.

decisions.description: Only what a person must decide before merging, one sentence each with the file and line it concerns. Empty when there is nothing to decide.

affects_product.description: true when the answer changes what users see or get; these are listed first.

summary_for_human.description: The detail for the run record (not the change request): what changed, what was contested and how it was settled, what the evidence shows and what it does not.
